claims.claim: You can apply for Funeral Support Payment online.
claims.quote: Apply online Most people take around 25-35 minutes to complete the form.
claims.note: The how-to-apply page explicitly offers an online form.

claims.claim: You can apply for Funeral Support Payment by phone.
claims.quote: Call Social Security Scotland on 0800 182 2222 to make your application over the phone.
claims.note: The how-to-apply page explicitly offers a phone application.

claims.claim: The applicant or partner must receive Universal Credit, Income Support, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit, income-based JSA or income-related ESA.
claims.quote: You or your partner must get one or more of the following: Universal Credit (UC) Income Support Pension Credit Housing Benefit income-based Jobseeker's Allowance (JSA), not contribution-based JSA income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
claims.note: The page names all six qualifying benefits and the income-based or income-related variants.

claims.claim: A person awaiting a decision on one of those benefits can apply for Funeral Support Payment.
claims.quote: If you or your partner are waiting to hear about your application for one of these benefits, you can still apply for Funeral Support Payment.
claims.note: The page explicitly permits an application while a benefit decision is pending.

claims.claim: A funeral director’s invoice is required for a Funeral Support Payment application.
claims.quote: To complete this form, you'll need: your National Insurance number details of the funeral director any travel receipts or funeral bills you have so far
claims.note: The application requests director details and any funeral bills already held, but does not require a director invoice in every case.

claims.claim: Applicants must provide proof of a qualifying benefit.
claims.quote: If you are still unable to verify the qualifying benefit, you must ask the client to provide two pieces of evidence confirming receipt of the benefit.
claims.note: Evidence is requested if Social Security Scotland cannot verify the benefit, not as a universal application requirement.

claims.claim: Being not yet on a qualifying benefit excludes a person from applying.
claims.quote: If you or your partner are waiting to hear about your application for one of these benefits, you can still apply for Funeral Support Payment.
claims.note: A pending qualifying-benefit application does not prevent a Funeral Support Payment application.

claims.claim: Another close relative who could reasonably pay excludes the applicant.
claims.quote: Whilst the nearest relative test should be considered in your decision, it does not necessarily mean this will determine whether the client should get Funeral Support Payment.
claims.note: A nearer relative is considered in assessing responsibility, but the source does not state that another relative’s ability to pay is an automatic exclusion.
